question: What does the permit-limit comment 'WHEN DISCHARGING' do to monitoring/limit applicability?

judgment.semantic_question_used: For Federal FY2025 monitoring periods, does evidence establish whether discharge occurred such that the pH minimum monitoring requirement conditioned on DMR comment 'WHEN DISCHARGING.' (permit limit row 3610840344|3600904607) was applicable?
judgment.interpretation: The permit authorizes intermittent backwash discharge from Outfall 001 and ties pH monitoring frequency to discharge occurrence via footnote *1 'When discharging.', which matches the structured DMR_COMMENT_TEXT 'WHEN DISCHARGING.' on limit set DISCHARGE BACKWASH WATER. Monitoring and the 6.6 su minimum pH limit apply only when the permittee is actually discharging backwash water; they do not apply during no-discharge periods. For Federal FY2025 (2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30), every monthly monitoring period tied to limit_value_id 3610840344 has a reported grab pH value and companion estimated flow for the same limit_set_schedule_id 3600904607, establishing that discharge occurred in each evaluated period and that this conditional monitoring requirement was applicable.
judgment.grounding: Permit NM0028762 final permit text defines Outfall 001 as intermittent flow and footnote *1 'When discharging.' for pH (STORET 00400) at 1/Week grab with limits 6.6–9.0 su. The statement of basis states pH shall be monitored weekly when discharging and describes episodic filter backwash (roughly daily to every three to four days). Structured row in sources/permit_limits.csv links limit_value_id 3610840344 to parameter pH, minimum 6.6 su (ME/MIN/>=), DMR_COMMENT_TEXT 'WHEN DISCHARGING.', limit set DISCHARGE BACKWASH WATER, schedule 3600904607. sources/dmr_measurements.csv contains twelve FY2025 monthly rows for 3610840344 with numeric pH grab results and no NODI, alongside non-zero estimated flow rows for the same schedule in each corresponding period.

snippets.text: 1. FINAL Effluent Limits – Outfall 001 – Intermittent Flow
Filter backwash using potable water occurs from once per day to once every three to four days depending on the plant and the time of year.
pH shall continue to be monitored weekly when discharging.

judgment.remaining_uncertainty: Discharge is intermittent (not continuous daily flow), so within any given month there may be days without discharge when weekly pH monitoring would not be required; the ICIS limit row encodes monthly grab frequency (01/07) rather than the permit narrative's 1/Week. This judgment resolves FY2025 monthly-period applicability from submitted DMR results but does not establish day-by-day discharge occurrence or whether all intra-month weekly monitoring events required by the permit narrative were triggered.
